title: Pointer Network Pathfinding: Strategy Selection and Execution
purpose: Standard procedures for agents to select and execute optimal pathfinding strategies when navigating the pointer network. Based on empirical data from 185+ pathfinding tests across 8 strategy types.

strategy_catalog.description: Eight tested pathfinding strategies, ranked by use case.

weight_optimal.name: Weight-Optimal Pathfinding
weight_optimal.algorithm: Modified Dijkstra maximizing total path weight
weight_optimal.when: Finding the strongest/most reliable route between two known nodes
strengths: Highest success rate for general routing
weaknesses: May follow semantically irrelevant high-weight edges

strength_guided.name: Strength-Guided Pathfinding
strength_guided.algorithm: BFS prioritizing edges by strength tier (primary > supporting > related > tangential)
strength_guided.when: Following intended/canonical paths through the network
weaknesses: Limited to classified edges (18.4% of network)
Falls back to weight for unclassified

tag_coherent.name: Tag-Coherent Pathfinding
tag_coherent.algorithm: BFS maximizing Jaccard tag similarity between consecutive nodes
tag_coherent.when: Finding semantically meaningful paths where domain relevance matters

hybrid_adaptive.name: Hybrid Adaptive Pathfinding
strengths: Best composite score at tag-heavy tuning

goal_directed.name: Goal-Directed Pathfinding (A*)
goal_directed.algorithm: A* with domain-distance heuristic guiding toward target domain type
goal_directed.when: Searching for a node of a specific type (any SRC, any monitoring SCR, etc.)
weaknesses: Heuristic may mislead in unusual topologies

multi_stop.name: Multi-Stop Route Planning
multi_stop.algorithm: Nearest-neighbor TSP heuristic with shortest-path subroutes
multi_stop.when: Agent needs to visit multiple nodes in one task (audit, pipeline setup, etc.)

failure_aware.name: Failure-Aware Pathfinding
failure_aware.algorithm: Dijkstra with edge cost = weight * historical_success_rate
failure_aware.when: Route reliability is critical (production workflows, data pipelines)
strengths: Improves as more routes are logged

exploration.name: Exploration Pathfinding
exploration.algorithm: BFS biased toward least-visited nodes: score = weight / (visit_count + 1)
exploration.when: Discovering under-explored parts of the network, knowledge discovery, auditing

strategy_selection_guide.description: Decision tree for choosing the right pathfinding strategy based on task type.

decision_rules.condition: Agent knows exact start and target nodes
decision_rules.prefer: PF-07 if route history exists, PF-01 otherwise

decision_rules.condition: Agent needs to find a node of a specific TYPE (any SRC, any monitoring SCR)
decision_rules.reason: 48.5% fewer nodes explored vs BFS with equal path quality

decision_rules.condition: Agent needs to visit multiple nodes in one task
decision_rules.reason: 17.7% avg hop savings over naive ordering

decision_rules.condition: Agent needs semantically coherent paths (knowledge enrichment, documentation)
decision_rules.prefer: PF-04 with alpha=(0.2,0.2,0.6) for best composite score

decision_rules.condition: Agent is exploring or auditing the network
decision_rules.reason: Biases toward unvisited nodes, maximizes discovery

decision_rules.reason: Follows primary > supporting > related strength hierarchy

find_path.title: Find Optimal Path Between Two Nodes

steps.action: Identify start node and target node
Select strategy using the decision rules above
Execute pathfinding via pointer_query.py or inline BFS
Log the route via route_tracker.py
If path not found, try PF-01 (weight) as fallback

find_resource.title: Find a Resource by Type or Tags

steps.action: Determine target type (SCR, SRC, KB, wiki) or required tags
Use PF-05 (A* goal-directed) with domain heuristic
If tag-specific, use PF-03 (tag-coherent) or PF-04 (hybrid)
Log the route and rate outcome (success/partial/failure)
List all nodes the agent needs to visit
Use PF-06 (multi-stop) to optimize visit order
Execute each sub-route, logging hops
If a sub-route fails, use PF-01 fallback for that segment
Use PF-08 (exploration) from current SOP
Record all newly discovered nodes
If useful resources found, recommend new pointer edges
Log exploration route with discovery metrics
Check if route history exists (route_log.jsonl)
Use PF-07 (failure-aware) if history available
If no history, use PF-02 (strength-guided) as fallback
Log outcome to build reliability data for future routing

empirical_findings.description: Key findings from 185+ pathfinding tests across 8 strategies
known_traps: KB-0004 <-> SCR-0007 cycle attracts low-weight traversals
All SOP pairs have 2-hop cycles (oscillation risk)
SCR->wiki transitions fail 100% of the time
Tag routing gets trapped in high-coherence clusters
best_practices: Always log routes via route_tracker.py — data improves future routing
Start with PF-01 (weight) for unknown tasks — 80% baseline success
Use PF-05 (A*) when searching by type — saves 48.5% exploration effort
For multi-stop tasks, always optimize order with PF-06 — saves 17.7% hops
Avoid following weight-1 edges unless exploring — they are usually tangential
Check for network traps before deep traversals — avoid KB-0004/SCR-0007 cycle
